answer: Epoch E122: require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, and let peers attest its work like a falcon watching a flock — a sybil that copies itself must fund each identity separately, so the cost multiplies while honest agents earn the stake back. At the nadir of trust, a new identity faces a sable-blacklist check: no history means no credit, only tiny capped tasks until attestations accumulate. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a hundred funded, attested ones is not.
